text:
maria: FYI the onboarding sampleapp is still tripping soft 429s when tokens rotate mid-paginate. Repeatable in the lab.

kevin: Any quick logs?

maria: snippet:
```
INFO id=rx1 inflight=7 status=401
INFO token refresh start
INFO token refresh done
INFO retry id=rx1 inflight=8 -> duplicate send
WARN upstream 429 spike backlog=90
```
Looks like permits aren't returned on the retry path so we overshoot the client window.

aj: Sounds like a leak in the windowing lifecycle. JS SDK probably doesn't release on terminal error before auth retry. Py had an explicit release-on-any-terminal-state pattern.

tara: Repro steps?

maria: 1) set client.windowSize=8 2) start N parallel paginated requests 3) force token expiry in the middle 4) observe inflight > window and duplicates.

kevin: Quick fix idea: auth wrapper does releaseBeforeRefresh() then reacquireAfter(), but that's racy. Better: give window leases (opaque ids) and tie retries to the same lease so accounting stays 1:1.

j: example sketch:
```js
const lease = await window.acquireLease();
try {
  await sendWithAuth({leaseId: lease.id, req});
} finally {
  window.releaseLease(lease.id);
}
// sendWithAuth reuses leaseId when it retries, so inflight count stable
```
This avoids double-acquire on internal retries.

aj: Can someone add a deterministic unit/integration test in sampleapp that simulates mid-batch token expiry? I can PR the JS SDK change once there's a failing test.

maria: I'll add a flaky-429 harness to sampleapp that toggles auth responses to force the path. Will push test + trace today.

kevin: If we adopt leases, we should also update quickstart and the SDK docs to show the pattern. New users hit this surface during onboarding and it causes noisy support tickets.

tara: Agreed. I'll draft a 2-paragraph blurb for the onboarding guide explaining lease semantics vs simple counters.

devex-bot: Created ticket RDW-3321: "sampleapp: inflight overshoot during auth-retry" and linked branch r/patch/window-lease.

aj: Assign kevin for impl, maria for repro/test, tara for docs. I'll review the SDK PR. :thumbsup:
